thread.title: Apple Tipped Cap About May, Time to Go Away, Says Bernstein

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Apple Tipped Cap About May, Time to Go Away, Says Bernstein
text:
Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein , one of two analysts cutting ratings today on Apple ( AAPL ), along with KeyBanc ’s Andy Hargreaves , appeared on CNBC’s “Fast Money: Halftime Report” with host Scott Wapner a short while ago to discuss his change in sentiment.
The cut follows Apple’s report yesterday of fiscal Q1 results that topped analysts’ expectations, but on lower-than-expected iPhone sales, and an outlook for this quarter that came in below consensus, as many had feared.
Sacconaghi, who cut his rating to Market Perform from Outperform, and cut his price target to $170 from $195, takes the view that Apple is stuffed with inventory of iPhone, and is about to disappoint similar to how it did back in 2015-2016 with the iPhone 6s .
On the segment with Wapner, Sacconaghi laid out the case that valuation’s simply “fair” now, given reduced estimates.
"Our estimates fell 8% for 2018 and 10% for 2019, and they would have fallen even more if not for an even better tax rate than many expected,” he said. "Our price target fell in line, and so we now believe the stock is relatively fairly valued."
But, pressed by Wapaner, he added the worry is this is headed for a disappointing number of quarters, like with the 6s:
We are a little bit nervous about the fact Apple built quite a bit of channel inventory, their highest build ever. During the iPhone 6s cycle, the company ended up drawing down the inventory, and disappointing over the next couple quarters. We are concerned that numbers are more likely to come down than to go up from here. Even though the valuation looks reasonable, we don’t see a catalyst for the shares to go higher.
Wapner asked how long the shares will be held back, whether years.
Sacconaghi said that’s not the case, saying his “near to medium-term” outlook applies to three to nine months.
"This is a dynamic company, with $14 billion in R&D,” he said “We don’t know what the new iPhone cycle looks like, or if Apple has something in its back pocket."
"Our best visibility into any tech stock is three to nine months,” he continued. “And we’re not calling for underperformance. We thought the shares would outperform. They have started to underperform, and we think the risk-reward is pretty balanced, so people should have a market weight in Apple."
When asked about expectations for a big increase in Apple’s capital returns program, something cited earlier on CNBC by Citigroup analyst Jim Suva , Sacconaghi dismissed it as not much of an event.
While conceding the “buyback could be a big one,” Sacconaghi nevertheless took exception, saying “bullish investors are saying they’re going to do a really big buyback, and my response is they already told us that last night,” referring to the conference call. During that call, CFO Luca Maestri indicated the company will deploy lots of cash into various capital allocations, as it seeks to bring its net cash balance of $163 billion to zero.
“It [Apple stock] jumped very substantially,” in the after-market, he noted, "as soon as they said that. It jumped by about 3%."
“And investors immediately said, We’re going to get a big buyback."
"My response is, we’re going to hear in May about a multi-year plan, but I think they tipped their cap, so I’m not so sure that’s a near- or medium-term catalyst."
Apple stock is currently down $5, or 3%, at $162.78.
